meta.title: Agriculture
meta.question: Should the state support farmers?
meta.measure: Average position on support for agriculture, from 0 (urban interests: no special support) to 10 (rural interests: subsidies and protection)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on agricultural subsidies and tariffs and the farmers' pension scheme (KRUS), with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Agriculture should not receive subsidies or protection vs should receive them
Agriculture should receive subsidies from the budget (0) vs should not (10)
State subsidies to agriculture (0) vs no subsidies (10)
items.notes: PGSW 2000 presidential study; the PGSW_AGRI_SUBSIDIES question.

items.wording: Agriculture should not vs should be protected by tariffs
The farmers' pension scheme (KRUS) should be retained (0) vs farmers should pay contributions in proportion to income (10)
Should all farmers keep budget-funded pensions whatever their income, or pay contributions like other groups?
The EU gives farmers financial support to stabilise their incomes. Is this support too low, about right or too high?
items.notes: Special Eurobarometer modules in EB 80.2 (November 2013) and EB 101.5 (June-July 2024). The question states the aid's share of the EU budget: almost 40% in 2013, about 30% in 2024.

items.wording: Over the next ten years, should EU financial support to farmers increase, decrease or not change?
To what extent do you agree with the farmers who protested in several European countries this year?
items.notes: EB 101.5 (June-July 2024), after the protests of early 2024.
